floor_history.headline: First honest pure-C measurement of motion_Close (floor 21->20, structure an exact match) — and a corpus-wide kill: gcc-2.7.2 o32 reserves REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE=16 for every C-level call, so the target'

Floor 20->17 from statement order alone; then H3 KILLED with the instrumented cc1 — global.c's allocno priority forces count->$s0 / p->$s1 for every C form that emits the target's instruction sequence

frontier.hypothesis: F1 (now the ONLY live frontier) — motion_Close's original source was hand-written assembly (PsyQ crt0 runtime), which is why its frame has no outgoing-arg area, its beqz delay slot is unfilled, and its register assignment inverts GCC's allocation priority.
frontier.mechanism: Three independent anomalies that GCC provably does not produce from any C: S-a the zero outgoing-arg area (REG_PARM_STACK_SPACE=16 forces >=16 for any C-level call; 854/854 census), S-b the unfilled delay slot (reorg.c fills it in every honest C form), and now S-c the inverted $s0/$s1 assignment (global.c's allocno priority is 30000 vs 20000 the other way). Corroborated by the crt0 neighbourhood (_start, InitHeap, a .word-syscall trampoline, bios_FileRead) and the ctor-table-walk body shape.
frontier.next_probe: Extract asm/funcs/motion_Close.s (absent — the function is C-routed, which is why tools/scan_hand_coded.py --single motion_Close aborts), then run scan_hand_coded to obtain a MEASURED signal tier. The endgame-lock canonical-asm gate requires STRONG signals (S1/S2/S6); this must be measured, never asserted, before any escalation packet cites it. Also re-examine the canonical gate's C verdict, which was reached on 'distance 21 <= 50' i.e. on size alone and predates every honest measurement.

frontier.hypothesis: The v0-vs-t0 scalar temp (2 of the 17 residual points) is separable from the s0/s1 role split and might move on its own.
frontier.mechanism: The guard load and the jalr target both use $v0 in every C form and $t0 in the target. $v0 is GCC's natural first choice for a short-lived call-clobbered temp; $t0 would require the value to conflict with $v0 across its live range. This is the one residual bucket session 2 did not probe directly (it was measured only as a by-product of the 27 spellings, all of which used $v0).
frontier.next_probe: Read the .lreg/.greg dumps for the temp pseudo's local-alloc disposition and check whether any C shape makes $v0 unavailable at that point without adding an instruction. LOW VALUE: it is 2 of 17 points and cannot produce a match while H1 and H3 stand — worth only as further corroboration for the F1 packet, and only if a forensics session is already in the dumps.
